links.outcome: Moderation API recovery of graded suicide risk severity versus high/low risk separation
links.effect: Moderation APIs reached 0.860 high-risk F1 but only 0.395 macro F1 for severity, and over-predicted the most severe category.
links.quote: Vendor moderation APIs separate low- from high-severity posts well (0.860 high-risk F1) but measure severity poorly (0.395 macro F1), systematically over-predicting the most severe category.

links.outcome: Effect of expert-authored clinical framing on LLM suicide severity classification
links.effect: Clinically grounded zero-shot prompting reached 0.562 macro F1 versus 0.395 for moderation APIs; expert-authored framing was the effective lever, not fine-tuning, reasoning, or multi-agent aggregation.
links.quote: Clinically grounded zero-shot prompting recovers much of that gap (0.562 macro F1), and expert-authored framing (not fine-tuning, added reasoning, or naive multi-agent aggregation) is the effective lever.

unlisted_practices: Measuring graded clinical severity rather than a binary flag for suicide risk
Matching reasoning use in prompts to text register (helps on short clinician-authored statements, hurts on long noisy posts)

screen.practice: clinically grounded prompt framing for suicide risk severity
screen.reason: Evaluates moderation APIs and LLM prompt strategies against a clinical suicide risk severity scale (C-SSRS) on Reddit posts, testing the effect of clinically grounded framing guardrails.

primary.practice: clinically grounded prompt framing / crisis severity escalation rules
